item.title: Explosion at Rotterdam port site kills one, injures several
item.description:
Explosion at Rotterdam port site kills one, injures several

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

One person has been killed and several others injured in an explosion at a site in the Port of Rotterdam, police say.

The blast happened shortly after midday on Thursday at a company on the Moezelweg in Europoort, regional broadcaster Rijnmond reported. Police said they had no further information at this stage.

Multiple people were injured and taken to hospital. Six ambulances, a trauma helicopter and fire crews were sent to the scene.

Rijnmond reported that a hired maintenance crew had been working on pipelines at the site and that something may have gone wrong as those pipes were being disconnected.

Traces of an explosion were visible on a storage tank, the broadcaster said.

Earlier on Thursday, a power cut shut down systems at the Esso refinery on the Botlekweg, sending large flames and black smoke over the port as gas lines were emptied. The Rotterdam-Rijnmond safety authority said it had not established whether the incidents were connected.

item.title: Amsterdam researchers find remedy for fatal child brain disease
item.description:
Amsterdam researchers find remedy for fatal child brain disease

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Researchers from the Emma Children’s Hospital at Amsterdam UMC have for the first time found a way to treat a rare genetic brain disease found mostly in children – vanishing white matter, or VWM.

According to The Lancet Neurology, which published the findings, VWM is a neurodegenerative disease “with onset mostly in children aged 1–6 years that causes early death and has no effective therapy.” It’s caused by a genetic defect and occurs in 1 in 100,000 people in the Netherlands.

But now the blood pressure drug guanabenz has been found to inhibit the disease.

In a trial at Amsterdam UMC, 33 children from various countries received guanabenz for four years, while the comparison group included 66 children who did not receive it. Children who received the drug stabilised and ended up needing a wheelchair less often and less quickly.

They also lived – as compared to five patients in the comparison group who died.

“We saw that the disappearance of the white matter in the brain slowed down or even stopped,” chief researcher Marjo van der Knaap told broadcaster NOS.

Moving forward, “the disease-modifying effect of guanabenz should be confirmed in a long-term extension study,” wrote the researchers. The drug also needs the approval of the European Medicines Agency to be used as a treatment for VWM.

item.title: Once-in-a-lifetime solar eclipse has Netherlanders over the moon
item.description:
Once-in-a-lifetime solar eclipse has Netherlanders over the moon

August 13, 2026 Lauren Comiteau

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Eclipse mania took over the Netherlands Wednesday night as people flocked to the coast, roofs and open spaces to watch the largest solar eclipse of the past few decades.

“It looks like a moon giving off light,” a woman on the beach in Petten, a village about 60 kilometers northwest of Amsterdam on the North Sea, told broadcaster NOS. “This is truly very special.”

Indeed traffic jams were rampant on the roads to the sea. But weather conditions were perfect for viewing the eclipse, which was broadcast live on NOS. Some of its broadcasters were clearly moved by the phenomenon.

“This is making me a bit emotional,” NOS weatherman Peter Kuipers Munneke said.

Underwhelmed

But others were less enthusiastic.

College student Sophie joined the crowds to watch the eclipse from the Marineterrein in Amsterdam Oost. Originally planning to make glasses out of old photo negatives, her friend managed to get hold of the hard to come by eye protectors in Amstelveen. But after all the effort, she said they were underwhelmed.

“It wasn’t that special,” she told Dutch News. “The moon didn’t even cover the sun fully. It was like 88% covered and all the sudden, everyone clapped and the sun came back. It wasn’t a total eclipse like in Spain, and it didn’t really become dark. But we had fun.”

A solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes between the sun and earth, blocking all or some of the sun’s light and casting a shadow over the earth.

item.title: Drought means less honey this summer as nectar dries up
item.description:
Drought means less honey this summer as nectar dries up

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The persistent drought in the Netherlands has now affected beekeepers, who have noticed that honey production is down this summer. Flowers are blooming for a shorter period, if at all, making it impossible for honeybees to collect the nectar they need to survive.

Professional beekeeper and secretary of the Professional Beekeepers’ Association John Hoogendoorn chalks it up to climate change. “There are increasingly longer periods of drought and higher temperatures, which changes the habitat of the bees,” he told broadcaster NOS. “Nature and the rich biodiversity have deteriorated over the years.”

He said the damage is particularly acute on the dry sandy soils in the east of the country, where the heather honey season has only just begun. Beekeepers report seeing dry shrubs and very little purple, flowering heather there.

Beekeeper Frauke Wessel from Haarlemmermeer has also seen the change. “The bees bring in food to keep their colony alive. But we notice that the honeycomb is no longer filled. The queen bee also lays fewer eggs because she does not get enough food,” she told NOS.

Honeybees need nectar to give them energy for flight and other daily colony tasks. They also convert any excess nectar into stored honey to get them through flowerless winters.

Because the honeybees can’t build up their winter supplies this rainless summer, beekeepers like Hoogendoorn are making up for the lack of honey with dissolved sugar. He told NOS that he needs about 15 kilos of sugar per colony this year to substitute for the honey shortage. “That’s more than in previous years.”

Bees are usually active in the country from the end of February until mid-September. “But due to the high temperatures, the bee season lasts longer and starts earlier,” said beekeeper Joris Knoops.

Flies, wasps, mosquitoes and dragonflies are also suffering from the lack of water.

item.title: Your takeaway habit is feeding Dutch inflation, says DNB
item.description:
Your takeaway habit is feeding Dutch inflation, says DNB

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Dutch households are spending so much on takeaway meals that it is impacting national inflation, the Dutch central bank DNB has reported.

Delivery meals have nearly doubled as a share of the average shopping basket, from around 1.6% in 2015 to just over 3% today, DNB said on Thursday.

Prices have climbed fast. With more people spending, delivery firms have also passed on higher wage, energy and ingredient costs, and between 2020 and 2023 the category went from adding less than 0.1 percentage point to inflation to a full 0.35 point.

It has since eased back to 0.13 point – but only because prices stopped rising so fast, not because anyone is ordering less, DNB said.

The bank traces consumer habits back to the Covid pandemic, when locked-down households began using ordering apps much more, especially while working from home.

Dutch inflation has sat above the European Central Bank’s 2% target for years, driven mainly by rents and food prices. The pizza and sushi deliveries are now also hitting the figures.

item.title: Monument against violence in youth care system vandalised
item.description:
Monument against violence in youth care system vandalised

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Just two months after it was unveiled, the national youth care monument (Nationaal Monument Jeugdzorg) commemorating violence against young people in the system was vandalised in Apeldoorn.

“This feels like a new attack,” Naomi van Aggelen told broadcaster NOS. She worked for years on the monument and was herself wrongly sent to live at a youth care institution when she was 12 years old.

“It is a very sad sight,” she said of the monument meant to acknowledge the suffering of young people in care homes. “Actually, [it’s] a denial of that recognition.”
Located in Apeldoorn’s Zuiderpark, the wings of the monument – titled De Erkenning (The Recognition) – were broken off and are now missing while scratches and dents are visible on what remains.

“Who does such a thing? We have no idea,” said Van Aggelen. “We don’t know where the wings are.”

The council has filed a police report and is said to be reviewing if additional security measures are needed.

The monument was commissioned after a 2019 report by De Winter Commission that found since WW2, some 20,000 children were the victims of violence in youth care. The organising foundation calls it a place of reparation, remembrance and “of vigilance: all current forms of violence must also stop.”

The future of the monument is still unclear. “I have no idea if we should leave the work for what it is,” said Van Aggelen. “Maybe we should glue it, then it symbolises another broken child in youth care.”

item.title: Barcelona legend Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach
item.description:
Barcelona legend Xavi appointed Netherlands head coach

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

Xavi Hernández has been appointed head coach of the Netherlands men’s national team on a contract running to the 2030 World Cup, the Dutch football association KNVB has announced.

The 46-year-old Spaniard succeeds Ronald Koeman, who stepped down after the Netherlands’ last-32 defeat by Morocco at this summer’s World Cup. His appointment ends a long and closely watched search, and comes as a surprise after several higher-profile names fell away.

Former Feyenoord and Liverpool coach Arne Slot, ex-Ajax and Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag and PSV’s Peter Bosz all ruled themselves out, while the KNVB passed over Jong Oranje coach Michael Reiziger and Louis van Gaal. On

Tuesday, Roberto Martínez was reportedly the front-runner, though the KNVB never held direct talks with him.

“A son of Dutch football”
Xavi becomes the first foreign coach of Oranje since the Austrian Ernst Happel, who led the side to the 1978 World Cup final.

“It is a great honour to become head coach of the Netherlands national team,” he said in a statement released by the KNVB. “As someone who was developed at the FC Barcelona academy, with strong influences from, among others, Johan Cruyff and Rinus Michels, I feel a special connection to Dutch football. You could say I am, in a way, a son of Dutch football.”

As a player, Xavi is regarded as one of the best midfielders of his generation, winning four Champions League titles in more than 750 games for Barcelona and lifting the 2010 World Cup with Spain – beating the Netherlands in the final – as well as the European Championship in 2008 and 2012.

He started out as a coach at Al Sadd in Qatar, then took charge of Barcelona in 2021 – also succeeding Koeman – and won the Spanish league title in 2023, but made little impression in Europe before leaving in 2024.

Restoring tactics
The KNVB has handed Xavi an explicit task: restore the attacking, possession-based football long associated with the Dutch game, after a World Cup exit widely seen as a low point in style as much as result.

“As a coach, he has been shaped by years of working with top coaches who share a footballing vision that aligns very well with the way we want the Netherlands national team to play,” said the KNVB’s director Nigel de Jong. He pointed to “taking the initiative, playing dominant and attractive football, combined with the flexibility required in modern football at the highest level.”

Xavi said he shared that ambition. “The Netherlands has a rich football culture and a clear vision that strongly appeals to me: attacking football, based on possession, with creativity, passion and conviction,” he said. “The main objective is always to win, but I prefer to do so in a way that reflects those characteristics and that people can enjoy watching.”

He will be presented at the KNVB’s Zeist headquarters on August 25 and takes charge for the first time on September 24, at home to Germany in the Nations League.

item.title: NL breaks 1947 heat record with 31 tropical days in a year
item.description:
NL breaks 1947 heat record with 31 tropical days in a year

August 13, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The Netherlands has recorded more tropical days in a single year than at any point since records began, after the temperature hit 31.5° in Maastricht on Tuesday.

It was the 31st day this year on which 30° or more – the threshold for a tropical day – was reached somewhere in the country, beating the record of 30 set in 1947.

Back then, the 30th tropical day did not arrive until September. This year the record fell in mid-August with weeks of potential summer heat still to come, and forecasters expect the tally to rise further.

The national weather service KNMI has linked the growing number of tropical days and back-to-back heatwaves to climate change.

The heat coincides with the second driest summer since measurements began in 1901 – only 1976 was drier – with the Rhine at its lowest in almost 80 years.

The public health institute RIVM has reactivated its national heat plan for the fourth time across the whole country from Wednesday, urging people to check on the elderly and young children and to keep homes cool.

Friday is forecast to be the hottest day, with highs of 33° to 37° and the chance of a fifth regional heatwave of the year, before cooler air moves in at the weekend.

item.title: Ukrainian soldier murdered by Soviets exhumed in Rotterdam
item.description:
Ukrainian soldier murdered by Soviets exhumed in Rotterdam

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

The remains of a Ukrainian soldier who was murdered in Rotterdam by the Soviet secret services in 1938 are being repatriated for a military burial.

Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, the founder of a Ukrainian nationalist group, was killed by a bomb concealed in a box of chocolates as he walked home from a meeting with an undercover agent.

The Soviet spy had infiltrated the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and handed Konovalets the chocolates as a gift during a meeting at a hotel in Rotterdam on May 23, 1938.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky announced on his official website that the colonel’s remains had been exhumed at Crooswijk Cemetery in Rotterdam so that they could be sent back to Ukraine.

He will be temporarily reinterred at the National Military Memorial Cemetery, in preparation for a farewell ceremony will be held at the Ukrainan Greek Catholic cathedral in Kyiv.

The OUN was founded in 1929 in Vienna as a right-wing nationalist organisation that aimed to establish an independent, ethnically homogenous Ukrainian state.

It was influenced in its early days by Italian fascism and German Nazism, but as Germany’s defeat in the Second World War drew nearer, the OUN adopted a more democratic ideology.

item.title: ABN Amro profit climbs to €781m as fees, lending grow
item.description:
ABN Amro profit climbs to €781m as fees, lending grow

August 12, 2026

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

ABN Amro has booked net profit of €781 million in the second quarter, up 29% on the same period last year and ahead of analyst forecasts, the bank said on Wednesday.

Analysts had expected earnings of around €686 million. The result beat even the highest forecast in that consensus, and shares in the group rose more than 5% to a record high.

The bank, which is now around one-fifth owned by the Dutch state after reducing its stake following the 2008 financial crisis, is in the process of a reorganisation that will cut 5,200 jobs by 2028.

The state is close to recouping the full €21.7 billion cost of the 2008 nationalisation of the bank, following a share price rally that took the bank’s stock above €40 this week.
